Analyst report · Q1 FY27 · Confidence medium

The Star Entertainment Group

The Star's Q1 FY27 (Sep-26 quarter) is the first positive EBITDA print in more than two years — A$12m (~$8m) vs –A$13m pcp — driven entirely by the two owned properties (Sydney + Gold Coast EBITDA A$35m / ~$24.5m, +164% YoY) and a 29% cut in unallocated corporate costs, partly offset by the Brisbane operator-fee reset (–67%). The operating turnaround is real but small: a ~A$48m annualised group EBITDA run-rate sits below our ~A$70m estimate of annual cash interest (currently paid from a restricted reserve), statutory operating cash flow was still –A$15.5m, cash fell A$28m to A$239m, and the day after the AGM the Federal Court imposed a A$260m (~$182m) AUSTRAC penalty that triggers a WhiteHawk review event. The equity remains a levered option on licence restoration and Bally's continued support, not a cash-flow story yet.

A$284m (~$199m)Group revenue (Q1 FY27)+2% YoY / +8% QoQ (pcp restated A$280m)
A$12m (~$8m)Group EBITDA+A$25m YoY (vs –A$13m); +A$21m QoQ
A$35m (~$24.5m)Owned-property EBITDA (Sydney + Gold Coast)+164% YoY; margin 12.5% (+720bps)

Analyst report · FY 2026 · Confidence medium

Atlantic Lottery Corporation

A flat year dressed up as a 50th-anniversary milestone: FY26 (Mar-26) net profit of CA$492.1m (~$354m) fell 1.3% YoY and missed the CA$502.4m (~$362m) budget by CA$10.3m (~$7.4m), the third straight year below target, as Destination (VLT/Red Shores) profit fell 7.4% and Retail lottery fell 4.6%, and iLottery's +15.4% (+CA$17.8m / ~$12.8m) was not quite enough to plug the hole. The real tell is Core Gross Gaming Revenue of CA$744.8m (~$536m), 6.1% below target and 4.6% lower YoY, while the illegal-operator leakage estimate was lifted from ~CA$200m to ~CA$250m (~$180m) a year — the grey market is growing at least as fast as ALC's online share (35%, +1pt). New Brunswick's review of licensing private online operators is now the dominant swing factor for the franchise.

CA$889.6m (~$641m)Revenue (gross sales less prizes)-0.1% YoY (-CA$1.3m)
CA$492.1m (~$354m)Net profit (100% remitted to provinces)-1.3% YoY; -2.1% vs CA$502.4m budget
CA$133.8m (~$96m)iLottery profit+15.4% YoY (+CA$17.8m)

Analyst report · Q3 2026 · Confidence high

ATG

A weak quarter on the only line that matters to ATG's owners: Swedish net gaming revenue fell 7.1% and parent EBIT 11.4%, dressed up by a 45% surge in Denmark that contributes almost no profit. The V85 experiment is being unwound (V75 returns 28 Nov) with NPS at -16, opex rose while revenue fell, and liquidity headroom is thin (SEK 15m / ~$1.5m undrawn) heading into a Q4 of restructuring charges. Cash generation (Q3 OCF SEK 499m / ~$50.2m) and 0.4x net bank debt/EBITDA keep this a sound credit; the open question is whether the incoming CEO can halt a four-year erosion in profit before owner transactions.

SEK 1,247m (~$125.5m)Net gaming revenue (Q3)-3.8% YoY / -4.2% QoQ
SEK 1,421m (~$143.0m)Total revenue (Q3)-3.1% YoY / -5.1% QoQ

Tennessee's mobile-only sportsbook market took $591.9m of gross wagers in September 2026 (+4.7% YoY; taxable gross handle $588.6m, +4.9%) — the best month of 2026 but still short of the $598.6m booked in November 2024 — and yielded $10.88m of privilege tax under the only handle-based regime in the US (1.85% of gross handle). Growth has decelerated hard from the World Cup-inflated summer (+30–38% YoY in June/July) to mid-single digits, the licensed field has thinned to nine operators, and the regulatory story is now enforcement-led (a Sixth Circuit ruling that Tennessee's Sports Gaming Act reaches Kalshi's sports contracts, and a run of offshore cease-and-desists) rather than tax or licensing change. For an entrant, Tennessee is cheap to enter but structurally rewards scale and high-hold product; it penalises promo-heavy or low-margin models because free bets are taxed at face value.

New York

September 2026 was a volume-strong, margin-weak month for New York mobile sports betting: a record-September $2.40bn handle (+5.0% YoY) produced only $159.4m GGR (-17.7%) on a 6.6% hold, the lowest September since launch, cutting the state's 51% tax take to $81.3m. Market report · 2026 · Confidence medium

Brazil

Brazil has gone from the world's newest large regulated online market (SPA-reported GGR of R$36.96bn (~$7.25bn) in 2025, 84 licensees and 193 brands by mid-2026) to a nationwide prohibition in 21 months: Provisional Measure 1.394/2026 barred deposits from 25 Sep 2026, took every site offline on 6 Oct and extinguished all authorisations on 25 Oct with no refund of the R$30m (~$5.9m) licence fees. The ban's permanence now rests on a Congress that had not even seated the MP committee as of 4 Nov, an STF rapporteur (Fux) who has publicly said he thinks bets should be banned, and a president re-elected on 25 Oct who is campaigning for the prohibition to hold. For B2Tech there is no lawful addressable market today; this is a binary watch-list jurisdiction until at least Q1 2027.

Brazil

Brazil's regulated fixed-odds market delivered a record 9M 2026 on paper — R$11.12bn (~$2.19bn) of federal collections from gambling and betting (+55% YoY) and an estimated ~R$30bn (~$5.9bn) of licensed GGR — and then ceased to exist: MP 1.394/2026 (25 Sep) prohibited all sports betting and online gaming, extinguished all 87 authorisations without compensation and took every one of the 188 licensed brands offline on 6 Oct. With Lula re-elected on 25 Oct and the MP still in force, the only routes back are the STF (ADI 8027, public hearing 3 Nov) or Congress (initial deadline 23 Nov, realistically Feb 2027); the credible reopening case is a narrower, higher-taxed, ad-free re-regulation in 2027, not a return to the 2025 regime.

Latin America

Latin America's 2030 story has split in two. The forecast houses still print a region of $51bn total GGR by 2030 (H2 Gambling Capital, Apr 2026) and $12.3bn of regulated online GGR by 2028 (Vixio), with a $467.6m online-poker niche (GVR) — but every one of those numbers pre-dates Brazil's MP 1.394/2026, which extinguished all 85 federal fixed-odds authorisations from 6 Oct 2026 and removed roughly half of the region's regulated online GGR (R$36.9bn / ~$7.2bn in 2025) at a stroke. Until Congress and the courts settle Brazil's fate, the investable regulated pool is Mexico, Colombia, Peru, Argentina's provinces and (eventually) Chile — a ~$5–7bn market with rising tax takes — while Brazilian demand migrates offshore.
